Rich.Colors.description: Colors and text styles are defined using style strings. These can be applied to any Rich renderable, such as console.print() output, table cells, or panel borders.

foreground.description: Specifies the text color. Can be a standard color name, a number (0-255), a hex code, or an RGB value.

background.description: Specifies the background color. Prefix the color with 'on'.

attributes.description: Adds text styling such as bold, italic, or underline.

combination.description: Styles can be combined by separating with spaces.

negation.description: Prefix an attribute with 'not' to turn it off.

link.description: Turns the text into a clickable hyperlink (if supported by the terminal).

color_systems.description: Rich auto-detects the terminal's color capabilities, but you can set it manually via the Console's color_system parameter.

values.standard: Supports 8 colors with normal and bright variations (16 total).[reference:0]
values.256: Supports 16 standard colors plus a fixed palette of 240 colors.[reference:1]
values.windows: Supports 8 colors in legacy Windows terminals.[reference:3]

standard_colors.description: The first 16 standard 8-bit colors. Note that these are generally defined by the system or terminal software and may not display exactly as shown.[reference:4]
